Question B-006-007-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Because an isotropic radiator sends equal power in every direction in free space, its three-dimensional radiation pattern is a sphere.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A torus (donut shape)": A torus is the familiar doughnut-shaped pattern of a dipole, with nulls off the wire ends, not an isotropic pattern.
- sourceIndex 2: "A cardioid": A cardioid has a favoured direction and a rear null, so it is directional rather than equal in all directions.
- sourceIndex 3: "A hemisphere": A hemisphere covers only half of space; an isotropic free-space radiator covers all directions around the point source.
